A request by the actor to launch another process. Refer to the launch_type_id attribute for details of the specific launch type.

A request by the actor to terminate a process. This activity is most commonly reflexive, this being the case when a process exits at its own initiation. Note too that Windows security products cannot always identify the actor in the case of inter-process termination. In this case, actor.process and process refer to the exiting process, i.e. indistinguishable from the reflexive case.

A request by the actor to obtain a handle or descriptor to a process with the aim of performing further actions upon that process. The target is usually a different process but this activity can also be reflexive.

A request by the actor to execute code within the context of a process. The target is usually a different process but this activity can also be reflexive. Refer to the injection_type_id attribute for details of the specific injection type.

A request by the actor to change its user identity by invoking the setuid() system call. Common programs like su and sudo use this mechanism. Note that the impersonation mechanism on Windows is not directly equivalent because it acts at the thread level.

The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events ( count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332 ). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.
description.zh-CN: UTC Unix 纪元毫秒，表示事件实际发生时间。

description.en: The CONNECT method establishes a tunnel to the server identified by the target resource.
The DELETE method deletes the specified resource.
The GET method requests a representation of the specified resource. Requests using GET should only retrieve data.
The HEAD method asks for a response identical to a GET request, but without the response body.
The OPTIONS method describes the communication options for the target resource.
The POST method submits an entity to the specified resource, often causing a change in state or side effects on the server.
The PUT method replaces all current representations of the target resource with the request payload.
The TRACE method performs a message loop-back test along the path to the target resource.
The PATCH method applies partial modifications to a resource.
The ACL method modifies the access control list of the specified resource.
The BASELINE-CONTROL method places the specified collection resource under baseline control.
The BIND method adds a binding to the specified collection resource.
The CHECKIN method creates a new version from a checked-out version-controlled resource.
The CHECKOUT method prepares a version-controlled resource for modification.
The COPY method duplicates the specified resource.
The LABEL method adds, sets, or removes labels on a version-controlled resource.
The LINK method establishes one or more links between resources.
The LOCK method acquires or refreshes a lock on the specified resource.
The MERGE method merges changes from another resource into the specified resource.
The MKACTIVITY method creates a new activity resource.
The MKCALENDAR method creates a new calendar collection resource.
The MKCOL method creates a new collection resource.
The MKREDIRECTREF method creates a new redirect reference resource.
The MKWORKSPACE method creates a new workspace resource.
The MOVE method atomically duplicates and deletes the specified resource.
The ORDERPATCH method changes the ordering of members in an ordered collection.
The PRI method appears in the HTTP/2 connection preface to confirm the protocol.
The PROPFIND method retrieves properties defined on the specified resource.
The PROPPATCH method sets and/or removes properties defined on the specified resource.
The QUERY method performs a safe query request that can include a request body.
The REBIND method moves a binding from one collection to another.
The REPORT method retrieves a report about the specified resource.
The SEARCH method searches a resource or collection using the request payload.
The UNBIND method removes a binding from the specified collection resource.
The UNCHECKOUT method cancels a checkout and restores the resource to its previous state.
The UNLINK method removes one or more links between resources.
The UNLOCK method releases a lock on the specified resource.
The UPDATE method updates a version-controlled resource to match a specified version.
The UPDATEREDIRECTREF method changes the target of a redirect reference resource.
The VERSION-CONTROL method places the specified resource under version control.

description.en: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. description.en: The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity. The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. description.en: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1 ).
description.zh-CN: 标准结果名称或来源的其他结果名称。

description.en: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code ( 0x18 ), an HTTP response code ( 403 ), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.
description.zh-CN: 来源产品报告的执行结果代码。

description.en: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code , such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts." .
description.zh-CN: 来源产品报告的执行结果详情。

description.en: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.
description.zh-CN: 来源操作的执行结果。

description.en: The status is unknown.

The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events ( count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332 ). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.
description.zh-CN: UTC Unix 纪元毫秒，表示事件实际发生时间。

description.en: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id . It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401 .
description.zh-CN: 由事件类别编码和活动编码计算。

A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source. Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.
description.zh-CN: 规则未使用且按平台策略保留的来源字段。
